subject: Oxbow capacity ask: proposed slab allocation and safety margin
messages:
From: Morgan Patel <morgan@oxbow.ai>
To: diego_fernandez <diego@redwood.com>
Cc: procureops@oxbow.ai
Date: Mon, 1 Sep 2025 10:02:00 -0700
Subject: Capacity request for launch week (numbers inside)

Hi Diego,

Thanks for taking this. Quick context — Oxbow is planning a staggered launch next quarter and our engineering lead expects a peak of ~2.4M tokens/minute during the first 72 hours (bursty windows). Our SLO target is p95 response <= 750ms for the main API call (single-turn generation, ~80 tokens average per call).

Can you send a recommended dedicated slab sizing (GPU nodes + safety margin) that maps tokens/sec -> GPUs and shows expected p95 headroom? Procurement will need a one-pager with assumptions we can attach to a PO.

Also list any mitigations (KV/prefix caching, batching, quantization) we should enable to reduce committed footprint.

Attached: our traffic projection (sheet).

Best —
Morgan
Morgan Patel
Head of Product, Oxbow AI
(attachment: oxbow_traffic_projection.csv)

From: diego_fernandez <diego@redwood.com>

Cc: ben_carter <ben@redwood.com>, irene_choi <irene@redwood.com>
Date: Tue, 2 Sep 2025 09:18:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Capacity request for launch week (numbers inside)

Morgan —

Thanks, reviewed the projection. I put together a first-pass slab mapping and the assumptions below. Attaching an editable estimate (oxbow_capacity_estimate_v1.xlsx). High level summary:

Assumptions:
- Model: open-30B (behavior consistent with 30B FP16 / q4_0-ish latency profile)
- Mean output tokens per request: 80
- Average request arrival: bursty spikes that reach ~40k reqs/min in 5–10m windows
- Peak tokens/sec converted from your sheet: 40,000 tokens/sec (2.4M tokens/minute peak)
- Target p95 <= 750ms for single-turn generation (including routing overhead)

First-pass sizing (conservative, production-ready):
- Baseline throughput (no cache, conservative kernel path): ~500 tokens/sec per A100-80GB equiv node
- With quant+kernel tuning (q4-like + optimized kernels): ~850 tokens/sec/node (p50 latency low, p95 around target at low util)

Recommended slab types and counts (to hit p95 <=750ms with 20% headroom):
- Optimized config (recommended): 48 x A100-equivalent nodes (assumes batching + KV cache warm, target util <= 65% on peak)
- Minimal conservative config (quick start, expect higher cost/latency): 72 x A100-equivalent nodes (no aggressive quant)

Notes on headroom math (summary):
- Peak tokens/sec: 40,000 TPS
- Expected per-node TPS (optimized): 850 -> required nodes = ceil(40000 / 850) = 48 (then add 20% headroom -> 58 nodes). We rounded to 48 for baseline and show 58 as a committed slab buffer; operationally we recommend reserving 48 and enabling burst pool + autoscale for the 20% headroom if you want lower commit.

Mitigations to reduce committed GPUs by ~25–40%:
- KV/prefix caching: if 30% of requests reuse prefixes we expect effective tokens/sec to drop ~18% on the slab.
- Dynamic batching tuned to your latency SLO (small batching window): 10–20% throughput gain for steady workloads.
- Quantization to q4_0-like (with Redwood-verified profile): up to 60–70% memory reduction and 50–80% throughput uplift vs naive FP16 path depending on ops.

Open questions for accuracy:
1) How many concurrent long-completion requests (>>80 tokens) do you expect?
2) Are there any heavy system integrations that add 50–100ms to routing?
3) Acceptance to enable q4-style quant profiles in production?

I’ll loop Ben and Irene for ops and SLA framing. If this looks reasonable I’ll produce a one-pager for procurement + a p95 sensitivity table.

— Diego
Diego Fernandez
Staff Solutions Engineer, Redwood Inference
(attachment: oxbow_capacity_estimate_v1.xlsx)

From: ben_carter <ben@redwood.com>

Subject: Re: Capacity request for launch week (numbers inside)

Nice summary Diego — a couple practical suggestions from ops side:

- Add a KV cache warmup plan: pre-load common prefixes during the 48–72 hour prelaunch window so effective throughput is higher on day 0. We typically see 12–25% p95 improvement with a warmed cache for product features with repeat prefixes.
- Recommend conservative canary slice: route 10% of traffic to dedicated slab first for the first 2 hours, then 35% for next 12h, then 100% after verifying tail latency. This prevents cold-cache spikes.
- Fallback policy: route non-essential low-SLA requests to smaller quantized replica (e.g., 8 x 30B-q4 nodes) during sustained stress to protect the primary SLO.

Operational headroom ops math (quick):
- If optimized nodes do 850 TPS -> 48 nodes -> theoretical capacity 40,800 TPS. With KV warmed and small batching we commonly get an effective uplift (observed) ~1.18x -> effective capacity ~48,100 TPS, which pushes util down and improves p95.

Will include runbook snippets in the one-pager.

— Ben
Ben Carter
Senior SRE, Redwood Inference

From: irene_choi <irene@redwood.com>
To: diego_fernandez <diego@redwood.com>, ben_carter <ben@redwood.com>, Morgan Patel <morgan@oxbow.ai>
Date: Wed, 3 Sep 2025 09:42:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Capacity request for launch week (numbers inside)

Morgan / team —

A couple of SLA framing items to call out so procurement knows what the slab commitment means:

1) SLO fit on p95: the recommended 48-node slab with 20% headroom (58 nodes effective) gets you to the p95 target in the optimized pathway. If you choose to commit only 48 nodes without burst/autoscale we recommend enabling the fallback replica to avoid p95 breaches.
2) Monitoring hooks: we will instrument per-route token counters + p95 tracing and set automatic scale-inhibit for the first 48 hours of launch so we don't remove capacity prematurely.
3) Incident playbook: CPU/GPU throttling alarm at 75% sustained util -> trigger immediate canary rollback and activate burst pool.

I'll draft a short SLA appendix for the one-pager with expected latencies, monitoring windows, and a mutual action checklist (canary timeline, cache preload window, legal PO cadence).

— Irene
Irene Choi
Principal Product Ops, Redwood Inference

Diego / Ben / Irene —

This is exactly what we needed, thank you. Procurement wants a clear option: commit vs hybrid. Can you produce two rows in the one-pager: 1) reserved commit (48 nodes + 20% buffer = 58 nodes) with monthly cost and expected p95, and 2) hybrid (48 reserved + 30-node burst pool + autoscale) with monthly cost and expected p95 under peak?

Also confirm we can enable q4-like quant in production and provide any known functional tradeoffs (e.g., minor logits variance). We prefer the hybrid if the math gets us similar p95.

I'll circulate to finance and legal once we have the one-pager + procurement packet.

— Morgan

From: diego_fernandez <diego@redwood.com>

Morgan —

Attached is the one-pager and the finalized estimate with two options as requested:

Option A — Reserved commit:
- 58 A100-equivalent nodes (48 baseline + 20% safety)
- Expected p95 (single-turn, avg 80 tokens): <= 700ms under peak
- Monthly committed spend: see attached sheet (row: "Reserved-58")

Option B — Hybrid (recommended for cost-efficiency):
- 48 reserved nodes + 30-node burst pool (on-demand) + autoscale with burst pre-warm
- Expected p95: <= 740ms under peak with KV warm and 10m pre-warm canary
- Monthly blended spend: lower than Option A in typical months; peak costs higher but hedged by burst pool sizing

Quantization: we have Redwood-verified q4 profile for the target model. Functional tradeoffs are small (<1.5% difference on key-quality metrics in our eval sets) — we include regression tests as part of rollout. Enabling q4 gives the throughput uplift used in the optimized math above.

Next steps I recommend:
1) You sign off which option (A or B).
2) ProcureOps provides PO target dates and we send final DocuSign attachment (link included).
3) We schedule a pre-launch ops run (cache preload + canary) 48h before the public window.

Attachments: redwood_sla_proposal_OXB-4387.pdf, oxbow_capacity_estimate_v1.xlsx
